name: lna-core-variants
description: First-stage core-variant study around design/lna_stage1: each declared change to the cascode core (not to the input network) is applied to the frozen netlist, and the issue-#74 network-independent bound (smallest NF any lossless input network can reach with S11 <= -10 dB, per frequency) is re-run on every variant over the same 27-point PVT grid (18 in-rail) and the DRAFT band, with the same probes, grids, thresholds and NF convention.
claim: ideal-element core-variant feasibility screen; no spec row is claimed met. Every matching element and the degeneration inductor are ideal lossless elements (no PDK inductor model; passive qualification is #46), the band (row 1) is OPEN/DRAFT, and the bound is a per-frequency necessary condition, not a realized network.

method._note: Grids (dense ac lin 71 over 17.7-21.2 GHz, ac dec 100 over 1-100 GHz), screen thresholds, tolerances, the 9 probe networks, the baseline (drawn) input network, the port fixture and the NF convention are all taken from the #74 declaration and executed by sim/lna-match-tradeoff/matchstudy.py unchanged. Only the DUT core differs.

_reproduction_note: The frozen core (variant core0) must reproduce the #74 record's per-point NF-bound max and Fmin range within this tolerance, and its jointly-infeasible frequency count exactly, at all 27 PVT points. Same ngspice, same models, same deck text apart from the variant comment line: anything above print precision means the comparison between variants is not on the #74 footing.

A.title: inductive emitter degeneration
A.description: An ideal inductor Le1 in series with Q1's emitter (between e1 and Re1). Degeneration adds a real part Re(Z_in) ~ omega_T Le to the core's input impedance without a resistor's noise, moving conj(Gamma_in) toward Gamma_opt. DC is unchanged (zero-DC-drop element).

B_J.title: current density at the binding corner
B_J.description: Rref retuned so Q1's collector current at hbt_wcs / 125 C / 2.5 V equals the Ka-band characterization's noise-optimal collector current for Nx = 8 at that PVT point (1.70 mA at 19.45 GHz, VCE 1.4 V; sim/hbt-kaband-characterization/records/20261009-095725-dbf8179.md, per-Nx table). The frozen core runs 1.43 mA there. Device size unchanged.

B_NX.title: device size at constant current density
B_NX.description: Q1 and Q2 go from Nx = 8 to Nx = 10 (the model card's upper Nx limit) at the same current density: Rref 8k -> 6.4k (reference current x 10/8) and Re1 3 -> 2.4 ohm (mirror emitter ratio Rer/Re1 = 24/2.4 = 10 = the new area ratio). The characterization shows NFmin nearly flat in Nx at fixed J_C while Zopt scales as 1/Nx; this variant measures what the size does in the circuit.

edits.line: Xq2 oc b2 c1 gnd npn13G2 Nx=8
with: Xq2 oc b2 c1 gnd npn13G2 Nx=10

edits.line: Xq1 c1 b1 e1 gnd npn13G2 Nx=8
with: Xq1 c1 b1 e1 gnd npn13G2 Nx=10

C.title: base-feed noise: larger Rbias with base-current compensation
C.description: Rbias 2k -> 10k cuts the base feed's shunt thermal-noise current by 5x in power. Its larger DC drop (Ib x 10k) is compensated in the reference by Rbr between the mirror's collector node nr and Xqr's base (the classic beta-compensated mirror), with Rbr derived so Q1's nominal collector current equals the frozen core's 1.563 mA (study.json derivation op). The mirror still tracks V_BE over process and temperature.

edits.line: Xqr nr nr er gnd npn13G2 Nx=1
with: Xqr nr br er gnd npn13G2 Nx=1

D.title: Rbias made noiseless (attribution only)
D.description: Rbias keeps its 2k DC value but its thermal noise is switched off (noisy=0). Not a circuit: it bounds what any base-feed change of class (c) can buy at most.

derivations.rule: Le such that Re(Z_in) of the core at node in2 equals z0 = 50 ohm at f0 = 19.45 GHz at the nominal point (the textbook degeneration condition), rounded to 2 significant digits
Rref such that Ic(Q1) = 1.70 mA at hbt_wcs / 125 C / 2.5 V (characterization noise-optimal Ic, Nx = 8), rounded to 3 significant digits
Rbr such that Ic(Q1) at the nominal point equals the frozen core's 1.563 mA, rounded to 3 significant digits
as le_a, on the (b, current density) + (c) core

selection_rule.description: Eligible: candidate or combination variants whose 18 in-rail points all have a valid bound (model check), pass the row-17 / card-box operating-point checks, have k > 1 and |Delta| < 1 in band and over 1-100 GHz, have transducer gain >= 10 dB (row 2 split over two stages, the #74 S21 screen) at the NF-bound source reflection at every band frequency, and have NO in-rail point where the bound is jointly infeasible (NF <= 2.5 dB with S11 <= -10 dB unreachable by any lossless input network at some band frequency). Choice: among eligible variants, the fewest declared changes, then the largest worst-case in-rail margin (2.5 dB - worst NF bound), then the name. No eligible variant: no choice, and the outcome is a decision-record proposal naming the binding corner. Excursion (2.75 V) points are reported and never enter the choice. Diagnostic variants are never chosen.
